26:1.sourceText: Ἀγρίππας δὲ πρὸς τὸν Παῦλον ἔφη Ἐπιτρέπεταί σοι ὑπὲρ σεαυτοῦ λέγειν. τότε ὁ Παῦλος ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἀπελογεῖτο
26:1.targetText: Agrippa said to Paul, “You have permission to speak for yourself.”  Then Paul stretched out his hand and began his defense:

groups.note: The dative σοι ("to you") becomes the subject You in English.
The article τήν serves as the possessive his.
The imperfect ἀπελογεῖτο ("he was making his defense") is rendered began his defense.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἐκτείνας, rendered stretched out, to the main verb began his defense.

26:2.sourceText: Περὶ πάντων ὧν ἐγκαλοῦμαι ὑπὸ Ἰουδαίων, βασιλεῦ Ἀγρίππα, ἥγημαι ἐμαυτὸν μακάριον ἐπὶ σοῦ μέλλων σήμερον ἀπολογεῖσθαι,
26:2.targetText: “King Agrippa, I consider myself fortunate to stand before you today to defend myself against all the accusations of the Jews,

groups.note: περί ("concerning") with the defense is rendered against.
ὧν ἐγκαλοῦμαι ("of which I am accused") is rendered the accusations.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render μέλλων ("being about to") separately; the infinitives carry the sense.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies to stand to introduce before you; the Greek has only ἐπὶ σοῦ ("before you").

26:3.sourceText: μάλιστα γνώστην ὄντα σε πάντων τῶν κατὰ Ἰουδαίους ἐθῶν τε καὶ ζητημάτων· διὸ δέομαι μακροθύμως ἀκοῦσαί μου.
26:3.targetText: especially since you are acquainted with all the Jewish customs and controversies. I beg you, therefore, to listen to me patiently.

groups.note: The noun γνώστην ("an expert") is rendered acquainted.
The participle ὄντα ("being") is rendered as a since-clause.
κατὰ Ἰουδαίους ("among the Jews") is rendered Jewish.

unmappedSource.reason: The τε of τε καί ("both … and") is rendered only by the following and.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of beg; δέομαι has none here.

26:4.sourceText: Τὴν μὲν οὖν βίωσίν μου ἐκ νεότητος τὴν ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς γενομένην ἐν τῷ ἔθνει μου ἔν τε Ἱεροσολύμοις ἴσασι πάντες Ἰουδαῖοι,
26:4.targetText: Surely all the Jews know how I have lived from the earliest days of my youth, among my own people and in Jerusalem.

groups.note: The particles μὲν οὖν ("so then, indeed") are rendered together as Surely.
The noun βίωσιν ("manner of life") is rendered how … have lived.
The genitive μου ("my") becomes the subject I of have lived.
ἀρχῆς ("beginning") is rendered the earliest days.

BSB does not render τὴν … γενομένην ("which was") separately.
BSB merges ἐκ νεότητος and ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς ("from youth … from the beginning") into one phrase; this ἐκ ("from") has no separate word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies my; νεότητος ("youth") has no possessive.

26:31.sourceText: καὶ ἀναχωρήσαντες ἐλάλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους λέγοντες ὅτι Οὐδὲν θανάτου ἢ δεσμῶν ἄξιον πράσσει ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος.
26:31.targetText: On their way out, they said to one another, “This man has done nothing worthy of death or imprisonment.”

26:32.sourceText: Ἀγρίππας δὲ τῷ Φήστῳ ἔφη Ἀπολελύσθαι ἐδύνατο ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος εἰ μὴ ἐπεκέκλητο Καίσαρα.
26:32.targetText: And Agrippa said to Festus, “This man could have been released if he had not appealed to Caesar.”
